article_title.ru: Гуманоид согласует шаги и усилия рук, толкая нагруженную тележку
article_title.en: A humanoid coordinates steps and hand effort while pushing a loaded cart
article_title.ja: 人型ロボット、台車を押す手の力と歩行を協調

caption.ru: Гуманоид толкает нагруженную тележку на ровном полу, согласуя опору ног и контакт обеих рук с ручкой; инженер записывает наблюдения. Редакционная иллюстрация к ForPC: робот, тележка и хват показаны обобщённо, без точной реконструкции установки Хуачжунского университета науки и технологий. Груз поддерживают колёса, а не руки робота.
caption.en: A humanoid pushes a loaded cart on a flat floor, coordinating foot support with both hands contacting the handle, while an engineer records observations. An editorial illustration for ForPC: the robot, cart and grasp are generalised, not an exact reconstruction of Huazhong University of Science and Technology's apparatus. The wheels support the cargo; the robot does not lift it.
caption.ja: 人型ロボットが平らな床で荷物のある台車を押し、両足の支えと両手の接触を合わせる。技術者は観察を記録している。ForPCを題材にした編集イラストで、機体、台車、つかみ方は一般化した表現であり、華中科技大学の装置の正確な再現ではない。荷物の重さを支えるのは車輪で、ロボットの手が持ち上げているわけではない。

alt.ru: Чёрно-белая гравюра: гуманоид стоит позади низкой четырёхколёсной тележки и двумя разнесёнными кистями охватывает её общую поперечную ручку. Ноги устойчиво опираются на пол, локти слегка согнуты. На платформе лежит прямоугольный ящик. Слева женщина-инженер в рабочем халате пишет карандашом на планшете; на заднем плане стена и окно лаборатории.
alt.en: Black-and-white engraving: a humanoid stands behind a low four-wheeled platform cart, grasping its shared horizontal push bar with two separated hands. Feet rest firmly on the floor and elbows are slightly bent. A rectangular box rests on the platform. At left, a woman engineer in a lab coat writes on a clipboard with a pencil; a laboratory wall and window form the background.
alt.ja: 白黒の版画。人型ロボットが低い四輪台車の後ろに立ち、左右に離した両手で一本の横向きの取っ手を握る。両足は床に接し、肘は少し曲がっている。荷台には長方形の箱が載る。左では作業着の女性技術者が用紙を載せた板に鉛筆で記録し、背景に研究室の壁と窓がある。

visual_thesis: При толкании тележки усилия обеих рук, равновесие корпуса и опора ног составляют одну физическую цепь; груз на колёсах не следует изображать поднятым руками.
visual_brief:
Use case: illustration-story. Create exactly ONE original landscape 16:9 editorial engraving for a robotics engineering newspaper, intended final width 1600 pixels.
Style: pure black ink on clean white, mid-twentieth-century Soviet popular science wood-engraving aesthetics combined with modern robotics. Confident contours, bold contrasting black shapes, disciplined moderately spaced hatching and crosshatching, strong clear silhouettes, white breathing space. Faces and hands remain light and readable at small newspaper size. No colours, sepia, toned paper, gouache, neon, ornamental border, readable text, logos, numbers, watermark or political symbols.
Subject: ONE coherent laboratory experiment, inspired by ForPC humanoid cart-pushing research. A human-sized modern humanoid robot on the left-centre PUSHES a low wheeled platform cart toward the right on a perfectly flat indoor floor. It does not lift the cargo. One plain rectangular box sits securely and completely on the cart's platform, centred within its support polygon.
Essential mechanics: cart is a SIMPLE rectangular low platform on four small wheels, with ONE sturdy inverted-U tubular handle fixed at the REAR edge nearest the robot. Two straight parallel vertical handle uprights are rigidly connected to the platform's rear corners; one continuous horizontal push bar joins their tops at about the robot's waist height. No second cart, no decorative rails, no extra handles. Near and far wheels share a consistent floor plane and axle orientation; caster yokes are simple and connected. Three wheels visible if fourth is occluded, never float. Robot stands BEHIND the handle, not beside or inside the cart; its forearms extend forward to the same bar. TWO clearly separated robotic hands wrap around the bar at two shoulder-width contact locations. Each grasp has opposed finger/thumb contact around the bar, fingers curve around its front, not vague hovering palms. Bar passes through neither palm nor wrist; both wrists connect naturally to the forearms; no detached fingers. Make the near and far grasp contacts visible with a slightly elevated three-quarter SIDE viewpoint. Both arms apply force to the same cart in the same direction. Hands do not grip the vertical uprights or the cargo.
Robot posture: plausible connected head, torso, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle joints. Simplified functional mechanical anatomy, recognisably modern humanoid but not an invented exact Unitree G1 product rendering. No decorative buttons or exposed cable tangles. Slight forward torso inclination, moderately bent elbows, knees naturally flexed, one foot a little ahead of the other with soles firmly supported by the floor. Stable pushing posture, no ballet stance, no impossible joints, no dramatic running or motion blur. The support/force chain is instantly readable: robot feet against floor -> legs/torso -> arms/hands -> handle -> rigid platform -> wheels rolling on floor. Box weight is carried by cart/wheels, NOT robot arms.
Human: one attractive harmonious woman engineer around forty with natural proportions, pleasant focused face, tidy tied-back hair, practical light laboratory jacket over trousers and flat work shoes. She stands well to the LEFT, safely outside the cart's path, at professional working distance. Concrete action: she holds a plain clipboard steadily in her left hand and writes observations with a pencil in her right; pencil tip visibly contacts the page. Her attention is directed toward the two hand contacts and cart, with her head turned slightly toward the experiment, not looking at viewer. No posing, flirting, romantic gesture, chin on hand, touching robot or secretly assisting its motion. She is visibly a technical researcher recording a test. No legible marks on paper.
Composition: wide three-quarter side view, full robot and entire cart visible including their floor contacts, human fully or nearly fully visible at left. Robot and cart are the dominant silhouette; the observer is secondary but active. Choose clear spaces between silhouettes so arms, push bar, handle supports, cargo and wheels do not merge. A restrained wall-floor junction and one simple laboratory window establish the room. No benches, hanging objects, gantry, poster or extra tools. No collage, multiple poses, ghost limbs, diagrams, arrows, UI, floating graphics or simulated screens. This is a conceptual editorial scene, not a photograph or exact reconstruction of the authors' hardware. It does not claim force sensors, precise payload, commercial deployment, slope climbing or obstacle avoidance. All significant elements must serve the single physical action. Prioritise simple accurate support and contact geometry over detail.
